subject: gamma prior for precision under target="stan"

messages.author: e4fb766a25afa573
messages.subject: gamma prior for precision under target="stan"
parts:
I have noticed some unusual results when specifying a gamma prior for a variance when target=“stan” as compared to target=“stanclassic”. I have seen this in a few situations. An example is given below, in which the analytical solution is known. Following on my previous thread about potential differences between using target=“stan” as compared to target=“stanclassic”, I am now using the development version of blavaan from github, as linked at the bottom of https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan.

 

The example comes from Levy & Mislevy (2016, Bayesian Psychometric Modeling), section 4.26. The situation is a model for a single normally distributed variable with known mean and unknown variance (or precision, or standard deviation). The model specifies the known mean of 80. The prior for the unknown variance is Inv-Gamma(5, 150); equivalently, the prior for the unknown precision is Gamm(5, 150). The dataset has 10 values: 91, 85, 72, 87, 71, 77, 88, 94, 84, 92. The analytical posterior for the variance is an Inv-Gamma(10, 534.5), which has posterior mean of 59.39 and posterior standard deviation of 21.00.

 

In specifying this model via blavaan, I wasn’t able to fix the mean. To get around this, I specified a N(80, .001) prior (in the sd metric) for the mean. And I attempted to specify a Gamma(5, 150) prior for the precision

 

Code for the model is:

 

library(blavaan)

test.data <- as.data.frame(c(91, 85, 72, 87, 71, 77, 88, 94, 84, 92))

colnames(test.data) <- "x"

 

# Define the model in lavaan expressions ------

blavaan.model.expressions.stan <- '

 

  # "Equation" for the model

  # This specifies a mean (intercept) for the variable

  x ~ prior("normal(80,.001)")*1

 

  # Variance for the  variable

  x ~~ prior("gamma(5,150)[prec]")*x

'

 

Fitting the model with target=“stanclassic” yields results for the variance that are in line with the analytical solution. Code and results follow.

 

fitted.model.stan.classic <- blavaan(blavaan.model.expressions.stan, n.chains=1, sample=50000, target="stanclassic",  test="none", data=test.data)

blavInspect(fitted.model.stan.classic, 'mcobj')

  

               mean se_mean    sd   2.5%    25%    50%    75%  97.5% n_eff Rhat

nu[1,1,1]     80.00    0.00  0.00  80.00  80.00  80.00  80.00  80.00 53383    1

theta[1,1,1]  59.52    0.21 21.04  31.37  44.82  55.29  69.53 111.39  9841    1

lp__         -22.92    0.01  0.99 -25.58 -23.32 -22.62 -22.21 -21.95 14025    1

 

Fitting the model with target=“stan” yields results for the variance that are meaningfully different. It seems there are more extreme values, yielding a larger mean, standard deviation, and higher percentiles. Code and results follow.

 

fitted.model.stan <- blavaan(blavaan.model.expressions.stan, n.chains=1, sample=50000, test="none", data=test.data)

blavInspect(fitted.model.stan, 'mcobj')

  

               mean se_mean    sd   2.5%    25%    50%    75%  97.5% n_eff Rhat

Theta_var[1]  71.16    0.29 26.83  35.49  52.50  65.75  83.59 138.68  8773    1

Nu_free[1]    80.00    0.00  0.00  80.00  80.00  80.00  80.00  80.00 54522    1

lp__         -26.02    0.01  0.99 -28.68 -26.41 -25.72 -25.31 -25.05 12963    1


I am unsure as to why this difference occurs. Can you advise?

 

Thanks,

Roy

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: gamma prior for precision under target="stan"
parts:
Hi Roy,

Thanks for the report, I missed a Jacobian in translating the SD to precision. It should now be fixed on github, and 1-parameter models should also be working (though 0-parameter models are not). I am working towards getting a new version on CRAN soon.

Ed
